negative_findings.description: The coverage cell names 'Мкх/national card scheme'. Searching in Macedonian for a domestic card scheme ('национална картичка шема', 'домашна платежна картичка', 'домашен картичен систем') returned no evidence of a four-party national card scheme in North Macedonia. The phrase 'домашна платежна картичка' refers to the 2020 government stimulus card ('Купувам домашно', ~324,479 recipients, ~EUR 28m), a prepaid social-support instrument issued via commercial banks — not a scheme.
negative_findings.result_summary: No national card scheme found; CaSys (Интернационален картичен систем АД Скопје) is a processor/switch, not a scheme. The 'Мкх' token in the cell brief could not be resolved to any real Macedonian entity.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prevents a downstream analyst from hunting a non-existent scheme operator and from mistaking the 2020 stimulus card for domestic scheme infrastructure. Domestic card rails in MK run on CaSys processing over Visa/Mastercard scheme rails.

negative_findings.description: Neither KIBS nor CaSys appears to publish transaction or terminal statistics on its own website. The KIBS site surfaces mission/vision, news, OneID, instant-payment and eIDAS/trust-service material but no statistics section; the CaSys 'About us' page discloses no volumes, client-bank list, or customer counts.
negative_findings.result_summary: The two actors with transaction- and terminal-level truth publish essentially no numbers voluntarily.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Volume intelligence for this cell must be sourced indirectly — NBRM aggregate statistics, Central Registry financials, MSE issuer disclosures, and executive interviews — rather than from the operators. Collection design should assume this permanently.

negative_findings.description: www.nbrm.mk .nspx pages returned HTTP 403 to a plain fetcher, and kibs.com.mk failed TLS hostname validation (certificate covers kibs.mk / *.kibs.mk).
negative_findings.result_summary: Both are hypotheses of bot defence / host-alias misconfiguration, not evidence of dead sources — kibs.mk fetched successfully, and nbrm.mk /content/ PDFs appear in search results.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A naive verification pass will wrongly mark the single most important statistics domain in this cell as dead. The collector needs a headless-browser or header-spoofing path for nbrm.mk and should canonicalise KIBS to kibs.mk.

negative_findings.description: Searches of Visa and Mastercard newsrooms and investor material found no North Macedonia country-level card, contactless or acceptance statistics. Mastercard's MK-specific output is the 2021 National Digital Identity Service launch with the government and NLB Banka; Visa material is CEE/global (Tap to Phone, contactless adoption) with no MK breakout.
negative_findings.result_summary: Global schemes are a partnership/product-signal source for MK, not a statistics source.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Sets realistic expectations: scheme-published MK numbers should not be planned into the data model; NBRM remains the only quantitative anchor.

negative_findings.description: No Macedonian-language term or local presence was found for American Express in the MK market. Searching 'American Express картичка Северна Македонија лиценца' surfaced only Diners Club material and generic acceptance lists; no local Amex licensee or issuing bank was identified.
negative_findings.result_summary: Amex appears to have no identifiable local licensee entity in MK; acceptance seems to run through acquirers rather than a domestic licence holder.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The cell brief assumes 'Diners/Amex local licensees' plural. Only Diners Club Macedonia is confirmed as a local licensee; the Amex half of that assumption is unsupported and should be flagged before any analyst builds on it.

negative_findings.description: No MK-specific SWIFT source was located. Searches surfaced SEPA accession material but nothing on SWIFT country membership, MK BIC directories, or SWIFT traffic data for North Macedonia; local-language terms for SWIFT are simply the English acronym ('СВИФТ'/'SWIFT'), which is too noisy to isolate.
negative_findings.result_summary: SWIFT-side MK data not found in this pass; SWIFT's own RMB/traffic trackers do not appear to break out MK.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Cross-border messaging volumes for MK will likely have to be inferred from NBRM balance-of-payments and MIPS EUR-leg data rather than from SWIFT.

coverage_gaps.description: Because nbrm.mk .nspx pages 403 to a plain fetcher, the exact download URLs, file formats (Excel vs PDF) and update cadence of the payment-statistics tables could not be confirmed in this pass — only their landing-page URLs.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run one headless-browser pass over nbrm.mk/platiezhna_statistika.nspx and /platiezhni_kartichki.nspx to enumerate the actual data files and their refresh schedule, then hard-code those file URLs into the collector.

coverage_gaps.description: Independent/non-bank acquirers, PSPs, ATM-network operators (including any independent ATM deployers) and terminal vendors serving MK were not enumerated. The cell focused on the switch/clearing layer and did not reach the acquiring-service and terminal-estate layer, which is where POS-count intelligence actually lives.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Pull the NBRM register of payment institutions / payment system operators and expand each licensee into its own source record; separately search 'еквајринг', 'ПОС терминали изнајмување', 'платежна институција дозвола' in Macedonian.

coverage_gaps.description: No supranational comparative payment-statistics source for MK was captured — ECB Payment Statistics / Blue Book style datasets, World Bank Global Findex, BIS CPMI Red Book, or IMF Financial Access Survey were not searched in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a targeted English pass over ECB SDW, World Bank Findex, IMF FAS and BIS CPMI for North Macedonia coverage — these give cross-country comparability that NBRM alone cannot.

coverage_gaps.description: The 'cash usage' topic was only touched indirectly (cashless growth percentages quoted in press). No source specific to currency in circulation, cash withdrawal volumes at ATMs, or cash-in-transit / cash-cycle actors was identified within this cell.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search Macedonian for 'готовина во оптек', 'подигања на готовина од банкомати', 'готовински циклус' on nbrm.mk and add the NBRM currency-in-circulation series as a dedicated source.

coverage_gaps.description: Several of the highest-value items are PDF series (NBRM annual payments reports, MIPS self-assessments, KIBS regulatory PDFs) whose URLs are long, percent-encoded and Cyrillic — fragile across site redesigns. No archive/mirror source (web.archive.org captures) was established.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Mirror each harvested PDF locally on capture and register a Wayback save for each NBRM and KIBS document URL at collection time.

coverage_gaps.description: Albanian-language sources were not searched. Albanian is widely used in North Macedonia and some institutional sites (including the Central Registry, which served an /sq/ path in results) publish Albanian versions that occasionally carry differently-timed or differently-worded content.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add an Albanian (sq) query pass for the same actor set — e.g. 'shtëpia e klerimit KIBS', 'kartela pagese Maqedoni e Veriut', 'sistemi i pagesave ndërbankare'.

brief: North Macedonia's payment infrastructure layer is a duopoly of intermediaries — KIBS AD Skopje (bank-owned retail clearing house, domestic instant-payments operator, digital-trust provider, and MSE-listed issuer) and CaSys / Интернационален картичен систем АД Скопје (the country's only Visa- and Mastercard-certified independent card processor, running issuing, acquiring, ATM and POS network management and e-commerce) — settling into the NBRM-operated MIPS RTGS, which has been dual-currency MKD/EUR since 2017 and is mid-migration to ISO 20022. The decisive finding for collection design is that neither operator publishes statistics: quantitative truth about cards, ATMs, POS terminals and transaction mix comes almost entirely from the National Bank's payment-statistics pages and its annual 'Годишна информација за плаќањата' PDF series, with operator economics reachable only indirectly via the Central Registry, MSE disclosures and executive interviews in trade and association media (mba.mk, bankarstvo.mk, ecommerce.mk). Global schemes are a partnership- and product-signal source for MK rather than a data source — no Visa or Mastercard country-level MK statistics were found — while Diners Club Macedonia (in market since 1996) is the one confirmed local three-party-scheme licensee; no domestic card scheme exists, and no local American Express licensee could be identified. The main access risk is technical, not legal: nbrm.mk returns 403 to plain fetchers and kibs.com.mk fails TLS hostname validation against a kibs.mk certificate, so both must be treated as bot-defended-but-live and collected with a headless browser and a canonicalised host.
